neighbours.label: An authority officially issuing or publishing something (' issued', 'publishes', the released notice/forecast/reference work); quiet when the same documents are merely used or described
fire: Driving licences in the province are issued by the transport ministry after a written exam.
A flood alert was issued for the lower valley early on Sunday morning.
Until 1971 the coins were issued in copper, nickel and silver versions.
Each spring the statistics office publishes revised figures for the previous year.
The health agency issued new guidance on vaccination for travellers last week.
Residence permits are issued at the town hall and must be renewed every two years.
The observatory releases a pollen bulletin every morning during the hay fever season.
Commemorative stamps were issued to mark the opening of the new railway.
quiet: Driving in the province is difficult in winter because the mountain roads freeze.
The flood covered the lower valley early on Sunday morning.
Until 1971 the coins were kept in a wooden chest under the stairs.
Each spring the statistics students travel to the coast for a week.
The traveller caught a mild fever on the journey home last week.
The town hall stands on the main square and has a tall clock tower.
The hay was cut every morning during the dry weeks of the season.
The children collected old stamps and glued them into a notebook.
